body.statement: Fix rational \(0<\varepsilon\le1/16\), rational \(T\ge1\), and \(M\ge1\). For each residue \(\ell=n\bmod8\), the actual finite allocation lattice \(\mathcal U_{n,\ell}\), its canonical interpolant \(\mathcal I_{n,\ell}\), and the fixed support-stratum charts in the finite-lattice coefficient extractor produce the displayed arrays \(f^2_{j,\ell,\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}\), \(f^D_{j,\ell,\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}\), and \(f^N_{j,\ell,\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}\). The three expansion families jointly satisfy \[\sup_{\ell,\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}},\,\|u\|_\infty\le M}|R_{n,\ell,\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}|\le C_{\varepsilon,T,\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}(1+M)^6n^{-3/2}.\] Their degree-six complete-risk coefficient equals one, their degree-eight risk sum is independent of \(\ell\), and it defines \(\mathcal J_{\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\). The quotient recurrence and chartwise bounds give, for every \(r\in\mathcal F_n(M)\), \[\left|\mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)-n^{-1}+n^{-4/3}\mathcal J_{\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(u_r)\right|\le C_{\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(1+M)^6n^{-3/2}.\] Consequently \(\Omega_{\varepsilon,T,M}^\dagger(n)=C_{\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(1+M)^6n^{-1/6}\) is the proved scaled finite-to-tube modulus. The same fixed-chart argument certifies every positive-count shell \(\mathcal S_{n,j}(M)\), \(0\le j\le J_n(M)\), and every zero-count face \(\mathcal Z_{n,A}\), and computes \(\Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}^\dagger(n,M)\) from the canonical width-\(2^{-n}\) interval maxima. By the imported parent orbit-game equality, unit averaging of every outcome-independent labeled design produces a count law \(\pi\) and uniform fixed-count conditional experiments. Under the permutation-invariant tube prior, the Bayes risk of every such design and labeled estimator is at least \[\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)\mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)\ge\min_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)=B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger,\] so the fixed-count bound applies to all dependent labeled designs. The effectively evaluable function \(\mathcal J_{\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\) has an attained finite supremum \(J_{\varepsilon,T}^\star\). Its finite-array formula extends effectively to \((\varepsilon,s)=(0,0)\), and \[|J_{\varepsilon,T}^\star-\mathfrak L^\dagger|\le\beta^\dagger(\varepsilon,T)=A_{\varepsilon,T}\varepsilon+B_{\varepsilon,T}/T,\qquad\mathfrak L^\dagger=J^\star(0,0).\] The schedules \[M_n=\lfloor n^{1/72}\rfloor\vee1,\quad T_n=2^{\lfloor(\log_2n)/12\rfloor},\quad\varepsilon_n=T_n^{-1},\quad G_n=\lceil n^{3/4}\rceil,\quad\delta_n=n^{-3/2}\] satisfy \(\Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}^\dagger(n,M_n)\to0\), \(\beta^\dagger(\varepsilon_n,T_n)\to0\), and \(C_{\varepsilon_n,T_n}^\dagger(1+M_n)^6n^{-1/6}\to0\). The exact target is \(\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)=n^{-1}\sum_tm_t\theta_t\) in every chart, and the coefficient saddle constructs a matching total finite primal procedure. No allocation count is omitted, and no differentiation of a moving lattice, moving factorial range, or nonintegral allocation is used.
body.justification: The root theorem is retained as the exact corrected-prior all-count bridge that would convert the finite experiment into the sharp unrestricted second-order value.
body.gap: The compact rational Airy approximation and exact finite evaluator do not imply uniform local, exterior-shell, or zero-face posterior-risk bounds; these must be derived with an effective common error sequence.
body.consumer: A prospective unequal three-regimen binary-endpoint design may use the proved fixed-design benchmark and same-input intervals now; the unrestricted sharp benchmark awaits this theorem.
body.proof_tex:
Assume first that \(\alpha_n(3T+2\varepsilon)\le 1\), so that the exact-primitives proposition makes every \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\) a probability distribution and hence makes \(\nu_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\) a genuine prior.  Conditional on \((X^\dagger,H^\dagger)=(x,h)\), the labeled response types are independent with common distribution \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\).  Indeed, if a labeled type sequence has count vector \(m\), then the multinomial-count probability times the reciprocal orbit size is
\[
 \left\{\frac{n!}{\prod_t m_t!}\prod_t
 \left(p_{n,x,h,t}^\dagger\right)^{m_t}\right\}
 \left\{\frac{\prod_t m_t!}{n!}\right\}
 =\prod_{i=1}^n p_{n,x,h,t_i}^\dagger.
\tag{1}
\]
This also verifies directly that the target under the prior remains the finite-population quantity \(n^{-1}\sum_i(c^\dagger)^\top t_i\), rather than its conditional prior mean.

Write \(\vartheta(t)=(c^\dagger)^\top t\).  The central types \(000\) and \(111\) have \(\vartheta(t)=0\).  The exact-primitives proposition gives
\[
 \sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^+\vartheta(t)^2
 =\sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^-\vartheta(t)^2=\frac58,
 \qquad
 \sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^+\vartheta(t)^2
 =\sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^-\vartheta(t)^2=\frac3{16}.
\tag{2}
\]
The equalities for the negative measures also follow by complementing every type, which changes \(\vartheta\) to \(-\vartheta\) and leaves its square unchanged.  Substituting the definition of \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\) and using the zero central contribution therefore gives the exact identity
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\vartheta(t_i)^2\mid x,h\right]
 =\alpha_n\left(\frac58|x|+\frac3{16}|h|\right).
\tag{3}
\]
The two specified polynomial densities satisfy
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E|X^\dagger|
 &=\frac{30}{16T}\int_0^T x\left(1-\frac{x^2}{T^2}\right)^2\,dx
 =\frac{5T}{16},\\
 \mathbb E|H^\dagger|
 &=\frac{30}{16\varepsilon}\int_0^\varepsilon h
 \left(1-\frac{h^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right)^2\,dh
 =\frac{5\varepsilon}{16}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

Now use independent assignment with probabilities \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\), and define the observable Horvitz--Thompson summand, its unprojected average, and its admissible clipped version by
\[
 Z_i=\frac{c_{A_i}^\dagger\{Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1/2\}}
 {q_{A_i}^\dagger},
 \qquad
 \overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i,
 \qquad
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}=\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}
 (\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}).
\tag{5}
\]
Every denominator in (5) is positive.  For each fixed schedule, the zero-sum contrast condition and \(q_a^\dagger=|c_a^\dagger|/2\) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_A Z_i=(c^\dagger)^\top Y_i=\vartheta(t_i),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_A Z_i^2
 =\sum_{a=1}^3\frac{(c_a^\dagger)^2}{4q_a^\dagger}
 =\frac12\sum_{a=1}^3|c_a^\dagger|=1.
\tag{6}
\]
Independence of the assignments across units and (6) yield the exact conditional randomization risk
\[
 \mathbb E_A\!\left[
 \{\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
 \mid y\right]
 =\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\{1-\vartheta(t_i)^2\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Averaging (7) under the genuine tube prior, and then applying (3)--(4) and \(\alpha_n=n^{-1/3}\), gives
\[
 \operatorname{BayesRisk}(\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}})
 =\frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left(\frac{25T}{128}
 +\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}\right).
\tag{8}
\]

The normalization of \(c^\dagger\) puts every target value in \([-1,1]\), so clipping cannot increase squared error.  Let \(\pi\) be the allocation-count law under this independent design.  Conditional on \(r\), its assignment is uniform over all labeled assignments with that count vector.  By the exact posterior square-completion calculation, \(\mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)\) is the minimum conditional Bayes risk in that experiment.  Hence the posterior-mean rule is no worse than the admissible clipped rule in (5), whose risk is no larger than (8), and
\[
 B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger
 \le \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)
 \mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)
 \le \frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left(\frac{25T}{128}
 +\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}\right).
\tag{9}
\]
The first inequality in (9) is the elementary fact that a minimum is at most a convex average.  By the definitions of \(B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\) and \(G_n(r)\), (9) is equivalent to
\[
 \max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}G_n(r)
 =n^{4/3}\left\{\frac1n-B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\right\}
 \ge \frac{25T}{128}+\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}.
\tag{10}
\]

For the prescribed schedule, \(T_n\le n^{1/12}\), \(T_n\to\infty\), and \(\varepsilon_n=T_n^{-1}\).  Therefore
\[
 \alpha_n(3T_n+2\varepsilon_n)
 \le 3n^{-1/4}+2n^{-1/3}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{11}
\]
so the positivity condition holds for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Equations (10)--(11) then imply
\[
 \max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}G_n(r)
 \ge \frac{25T_n}{128}+\frac{15}{256T_n}
 \longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{12}
\]

Finally, the local and shell conclusions in the original claim would imply the opposite.  On \(\mathcal F_n(M_n)\), multiplying the proposed local remainder bound by \(n^{4/3}\) gives
\(G_n(r)\le J_{\varepsilon_n,T_n}^\star+
\Omega_{\varepsilon_n,T_n,M_n}^\dagger(n)\).  On every exterior shell or zero-count face, outwardness of \(\overline G\) and \(\underline J^\star\), together with the definition of \(\Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}^\dagger\), gives
\(G_n(r)\le J_{\varepsilon_n,T_n}^\star+
\Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}^\dagger(n,M_n)\).  Those sets partition \(\mathcal R_{n,3}\), whence
\[
 \max_rG_n(r)\le J_{\varepsilon_n,T_n}^\star+
 \max\!\left\{
 \Omega_{\varepsilon_n,T_n,M_n}^\dagger(n),
 \Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}^\dagger(n,M_n)\right\}.
\tag{13}
\]
The claimed tube-removal bound and the three claimed vanishing moduli would make the right side of (13) converge to the finite number \(\mathfrak L^\dagger\), contradicting (12).  Thus (10) is an exact early-kill certificate: the widening polynomial density \(w_T\) cannot support the asserted finite tube-removal limit.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove a computable diagonal \(k_n\uparrow\infty\), \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\downarrow0\) for the corrected Airy-tube prior whose fixed-count Bayes deficits are bounded by \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+o(1)\) uniformly on the local \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation face, every positive-count exterior shell, and every zero-count face, and combine it with a matching total finite primal construction.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen coefficient extractor only names formal arrays; it supplies no proved Taylor, Euler--Maclaurin, posterior-denominator, or quotient bound for the corrected spline density. Same-input exact enumeration gives no cross-sample modulus. In particular, neither boundary allocations nor the design optimization can be discarded, and the old polynomial family is impossible because its exact deficit diverges with \(T_n\).
obligation.attempted: The former widening family was stress-tested by an independent Horvitz--Thompson Bayes-risk calculation and refuted. It was replaced by compact rational spline squares converging to the Airy ground-state density while preserving the nonzero transverse response measure. The corrected prior was carried through exact positivity, finite-population target, permutation-orbit, posterior square-completion, and finite ordered-algebraic evaluation arguments. These steps do not yield the required uniform likelihood expansion.
obligation.partial_result: The widening-density contradiction is exact.  The replacement amplitudes \(\varphi_k^\dagger\) converge to the Airy ground state in weighted \(H^1\), have exact rational piecewise-polynomial densities, and obey the certified energy bound.  For every fixed admissible \((n,k,\varepsilon,\delta)\), the corrected prior is genuine, its all-design permutation-orbit Bayes reduction is exact, and a terminating ordered-algebraic evaluator returns a same-input risk interval.  Independently, the fixed allocation \(q^\dagger\) has second-order value \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), and the unrestricted deficit has lower limit at least that value.
